chapter: Donaldsonville, family and Richard M. Jones
title: Richard M. Jones's songs
summary: Allen asks about Jazzin' Baby Blues, Trouble in Mind and Riverside Blues; Jones knows only the sheet music of Real Red Wagon.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: Mm-hmm. Did you ever hear Jazz and Baby's blues? Yeah, I heard them all. Yeah. Mushmouth blues? What? Mushmouth? I don't know. I don't know. You don't remember it, huh?
Mm-hmm. It'd be nice if you could find some of those things if you'd like to look at them, you know.
What about Trouble in Mind? Did you ever hear that one? That's him. That's him. That's him.

Oh yeah, I don't know who it is. I heard it sung by so many people. I got some of them all. Mm-hmm. I heard it by so many people singing that, you know. Oh yeah. I mean, recorded by so many people. But I heard the same song by him. You heard him singing, huh? Mm-hmm. He sang all his numbers up there too. I call it the Bulls.
Mm-hmm. What about Riverside Blues? Do you know that number?
Well, the only thing that I have music on is Real Red Wagon. He sent me that. And something else, you know how they write those piano copies. The only backup there is another tune.
